newsitem.title: USA: Emerging markets paper off but Russian debt higher.
newsitem.headline: Emerging markets paper off but Russian debt higher.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were mostly lower on profit-taking in the late afternoon, but traders said Russian debt managed to extend gains posted earlier this week following positive ratings news.

"Russia traded up very strongly on higher-than-expected ratings and traded off (earlier Wednesday) on rumors of (Russian President Boris) Yeltsin's death, but it has since stabilized to about where we were yesterday," said one emerging markets debt trader at a major U.S. investment bank.
Russian Vnesh dollar loans rose 1/4 to 79-1/2, furthering Tuesday's 1-1/4-point gain.
One emerging markets debt expert explained that the stellar performance of Russian loans this week was actually a repricing of spreads to those of comparably rated U.S. high-yield bonds.

"If you look at where comparably rated high-yield bonds trade, Russia still looks extremely cheap, so you are seeing a big repricing of Russia up to those levels," the source said, noting that a similar trend is emerging in the broader market.

"The dominant theme in the market right now is what I call high-yield convergence. What you are seeing with Russia is a confirmation of what is going on overall in the market. We are seeing the same thing happen in Panama."
On Monday, Moody's Investors Service assigned a Ba2 rating to Russia's long-term foreign-currency bonds, Standard and Poor's gave a BB-minus rating and IBCA gave a BBplus rating.
Elsewhere, traders said the market continued to await pricing of Brazil's bond issue, which some estimate could be as big as $1.0 billion and may be priced by the end of the week.

"Brazil came out with a Petrobras deal today and they are looking at a sovereign over the next couple of days, so we had a very good bid over the last couple of days in Brazil," said another emerging markets debt source.

In the broader market, traders said a bout of profit-taking and lower U.S. Treasury bond prices sent emerging market debt prices mostly lower. Brazilian C bonds slipped 1/4 to 72-3/4 bid, Argentine FRBs fell 1/2 to 84-1/8 bid and Mexico's UMS-26 bonds eased 1/4 to 102-1/4.
At 1652 EDT/2152 GMT, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was off 11/32 at 98-30/32 to yield 6.83 percent.

"The Dow is having a tough time getting through 6000 so the (Treasury) bonds sold off a bit so the (emerging debt) market is tired here. It has come a long way so there is always a period of profit-taking and consolidation," one said.
